written: 2026-11-21, after SeedLM-24, before the measure was run
theory: A right program is what the coder would write for the description on any example of the task. A wrong program that fits the visible example by accident is the coder's answer only for that example; asked to explain its own outputs on other inputs, it should look less like the description's program. Scoring a candidate as the coder's answer to several examples (the visible one and pseudo-examples made from the candidate's own outputs) turns one example into several without any hidden information
rule: for each verified program in a coder's width-32 beam (up to 8; SeedLM-24's held-out candidate files), the sum of the coder's log-probabilities of that program for the visible example and for three pseudo-examples (the first three probe inputs on which it runs, with its own output); the highest sum is chosen, ties to beam order. Tasks whose candidates use the visible output string (o, o!) keep the coder's first program (scripts/seedlm25_cycle.py)
primary_measure: held-out teacher tasks (139): tasks right with the rule's choice minus with the coder's first verified program, mean over s12-a1, s12-a2, s12-a3. Supported if at least +4; not supported if at most +1; inconclusive otherwise
secondary_measures: fixed and broken tasks; the ceiling (some verified program right)
the pseudo-examples alone, without the visible example (reported, not chosen)
choice: diagnostic; if supported, the rule is next tried inside the coder ensemble and with the engine, each pre-registered

outcome.primary: held-out teacher tasks, the rule's choice minus the coder's first: s12-a1 59 vs 59, s12-a2 59 vs 59, s12-a3 63 vs 62; mean +0.33: not supported (reports/seedlm/cycle_rerank.json)
secondary: development fifth: 56 vs 56, 52 vs 53, 57 vs 58; mean -0.67
the rule changed the choice on 5, 11, 10 teacher tasks (fixing 1, 1, 1; breaking 1, 1, 0); 20 to 23 teacher tasks kept the first program because their candidates use the output string
outcome.reading: The coder's first program is almost always also the program it finds most likely for its own outputs on other inputs. Its wrong first choices are not accidents of the one example; they are its reading of the description, stable when it re-reads with other examples. Only a reader that reads differently (another coder) disagrees with them
